- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and model is overconfident (high forecast), reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion.  
- When true outcome is below 65% of historical mean, model often overcorrects upward; apply downward bias correction.  
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to overfit short-term trends; smooth forecast by 1–2% downward.
